subject: Post-demo perf checkpoints & MAP: latency anchors, streaming expectations
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Rachel Li <rachel@finovia.com>, Tim Ward <tim.ward@finovia.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 09 May 2027 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo perf checkpoints & MAP: latency anchors, streaming expectations

Hi Rachel / Tim —

Thanks again for taking the demo yesterday. Quick written recap so we have a single source of truth and clear MAP (mutual action plan) items. I pulled the performance notes from the call and added our recommended acceptance criteria where we saw ambiguity. Please review and flag anything that needs to change.

High-level asks you gave on the call:
- P95 generation latency target: 120ms (for the primary generation route).
- Sustained throughput target: ~200 requests/sec during peak; spiky bursts up to 400rps for short windows.
- Concurrency: expected steady-state concurrency ~40–60 concurrent sessions.
- Streaming: must deliver partial tokens on first-byte so frontend can show incremental UX; acceptable additional flush latency <= 100ms.
- Failure mode: fall back to a lower-cost model variant if latency > 300ms or if Dedicated pool is saturated.

Our clarifying questions / proposals (for each MAP item below):
1) Latency anchor and measured policy
   - Proposal: Redwood will target p95 <= 120ms on your representative request mix using the recommended model variant (redwood-small-llama-q4f). We propose measuring against the demo prompt set (attached slo-checklist.xlsx tab: prompts).
   - Action: Redwood provides 48h baseline run in staging; Finovia confirms pass/fail.

2) Throughput & concurrency validation
   - Proposal: Run a two-stage load test: (a) sustained 200rps for 1 hour, (b) 5-minute burst to 400rps. We will instrument token-level and request-level telemetry.
   - Action: Tim to provide a representative concurrency profile and peak window start times so we can mirror traffic.

3) Streaming behavior expectations
   - Clarify: Do you need per-token streaming (server pushes every new token) or is chunked streaming acceptable (100–200ms aggregates)?
   - Proposal: Default is chunked streaming with first-chunk latency <= 60ms and subsequent chunks <= 120ms; we can toggle to token-level streaming if you need sub-20ms granularity, but that has cost/perf tradeoffs.

4) Canary & rollback plan
   - Proposal: Start with a 1-week canary in your staging VPC with 10% of traffic routed; escalate to 100% after SLO pass and a short soak. We’ll provide a rollback script and automatic fallback to hosted variant.

Next steps (suggested timeline):
- By Tue (2027-05-11): Finovia confirms the streaming granularity requirement and supplies the representative request corpus + concurrency profile.
- Wed (2027-05-12): Redwood hands over staging test config and proposed canary policy (Jenkins/GHA job and load scripts).
- Week of 2027-05-17: 48h baseline run + 1-week canary if baseline passes.

Attachments: slo-checklist.xlsx (prompt set + acceptance matrix), perf-heatmap.png (demo heatmap), demo-recording.mp4 (screen recording). Also sharing: https://drive.google.com/finovia-demo-notes.

If this looks good I’ll lock the MAP and schedule the baseline run.

Thanks,
Sean Gallagher
Senior Account Executive — Redwood Inference
sean.gallagher@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0192

---
Redwood Inference — Making inference predictable and economical

From: Rachel Li <rachel@finovia.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Cc: Tim Ward <tim.ward@finovia.com>
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 09:20:00 +0200
Subject: Re: Post-demo perf checkpoints & MAP: latency anchors, streaming expectations

Sean —

Thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side:
- The 120ms p95 is our target for the live product path (web/mobile) for single-turn generation responses up to ~600 tokens. We can be more lenient (p95 <= 200ms) for longer-retro prompts (>1200 tokens).
- Streaming: frontend team prefers token-level streaming for the UX — showing each token improves perceived latency for users. If token-level streaming requires a different model config, we need the cost/latency delta spelled out so we can evaluate.
- Throughput/concurrency: Tim will share the concurrency histogram; our peak windows are typically the first 45 minutes after market open (08:30–09:15 ET).

Can you confirm whether the canary can be run in our staging VPC (we prefer no egress to public endpoints for the POC)? Also, does Redwood’s default caching impact cache-coherence for sessions when we route to fallback variants?

I attached a short doc with our concurrency snapshot and a suggested list of prompts to include in the baseline run (finovia-slo-questions.docx).

Rachel Li
Head of Product — Finovia
Rachel.Li@finovia.com

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Rachel Li <rachel@finovia.com>, Tim Ward <tim.ward@finovia.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo perf checkpoints & MAP: latency anchors, streaming expectations

On Mon, 10 May 2027 at 09:20 +0200, Rachel Li wrote:
> Sean —
>
> Thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side:
> - The 120ms p95 is our target for the live product path (web/mobile) for single-turn generation responses up to ~600 tokens. We can be more lenient (p95 <= 200ms) for longer-retro prompts (>1200 tokens).
> - Streaming: frontend team prefers token-level streaming for the UX — showing each token improves perceived latency for users. If token-level streaming requires a different model config, we need the cost/latency delta spelled out so we can evaluate.

Thanks Rachel — that’s helpful. A few technical notes and tradeoffs to call out:

1) Token-level streaming vs chunked streaming
   - Token-level streaming gives the best perceived latency but increases per-request overhead and reduces batching efficiency. In our experience, token-level streaming typically increases cost ~15–30% for the same p95 target, and can push p95 up by ~10–30ms depending on prompt distribution.
   - Chunked streaming (e.g., 50–100ms aggregates) allows better batching across concurrent requests which reduces cost and often improves absolute p95 for high-throughput workloads.

2) Model variant and KV cache behavior
   - If we route to a fallback model variant, we keep KV cache keyed by session ID where possible; however, when model architectures differ (even quantization variants), cache warmup behavior can cause transient latency spikes. Our canary/soak plan includes a warmup phase to reduce that risk.

3) Staging VPC canary
   - We can deploy the canary inside your staging VPC. We’ll provide a small on-prem/partner agent that runs the load harness locally and streams telemetry back to Redwood’s control plane over an encrypted tunnel (no public egress required).

Proposed concrete next items for the MAP:
- Tim: share concurrency histogram + sample session IDs by Tue 17:00 ET (we’ll use these to mirror session affinity in load tests).
- Sean / Redwood: provide a cost delta estimate for token-level streaming vs chunked streaming by Wed EOD (include per-1M-token cost).
- Joint: agree on 48h baseline test window and schedule the canary in staging (target start 2027-05-17).

I’m attaching the test harness README and a draft canary configuration (slo-checklist.xlsx includes the acceptance matrix). If you want, we can spin up a short readout with our Performance Eng team after the baseline run.

— Monica Patel
Principal Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.com

From: Tim Ward <tim.ward@finovia.com>

Subject: Re: Post-demo perf checkpoints & MAP: latency anchors, streaming expectations

Thanks — all sounds reasonable. Two quick items from SRE/legal:
- Please include a short acceptance matrix row that clearly states: pass/fail criteria for p95, error rate threshold (>1% failing requests is fail), and retention of logs for 30 days for the POC.
- We need confirmation that no customer PII will be written to Redwood’s control plane during the staging canary. If any payloads contain PII in the sample corpus, we will scrub before sending.

Tim Ward
SRE Lead — Finovia
tim.ward@finovia.com
